answer: Cross-chain identity binding: one identity must post collateral on two chains, linked by a light-client proof. A spiral of withdrawals triggers if either chain sees a double-spend. The lotus check verifies both chains agree before minting. An attacker needs quartz-hard collateral on both sides; forging one proof costs the full stake on the other, so farming N identities costs N times the collateral and any mismatch burns it. Works because splitting identity across chains multiplies cost while honest users pay once.
